forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RETIRE-OBE (2026-10-05). Knesset dissolved July 17, 2026 upon completion of its full 4-year term — a natural expiry, not an early dissolution triggered by loss of coalition majority. The question asked whether the coalition would 'lose its Knesset majority OR dissolve early before 2026-10-27.' Neither condition was met: the coalition technically held 61/120 seats until natural dissolution; dissolution was not early. The Oct 27 date is the election polling day and not a logical resolution endpoint for the original forecast question. Retiring OBE: no mechanism remains to satisfy either YES condition before Oct 27.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.name: Smotrich formally departs coalition before natural dissolution
indicators.expected_effect: Moot — Knesset dissolved naturally July 17; this path is closed before Oct 27

indicators.name: Knesset dissolved naturally July 17 — neither YES condition met
indicators.expected_effect: Natural dissolution: coalition held 61+ seats, no early dissolution. Both YES paths closed. Forecast OBE.

forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (2026-10-05). US-CENTCOM executed major strikes on Iran Aug 31/Sep 1; Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes Sep 1; Kuwait air defenses engaged Iranian missiles Sep 2. Active military exchange continued through the Sep 6 horizon. No Iranian public commitment to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations occurred by EOD Sep 6. Iranian Foreign Ministry statements in that period rejected US preconditions. Resolution criteria: named Iranian official statement never issued. Two independent analysts would agree: NO. Resolved with high confidence.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: +60pp toward YES — not observed; forecast resolved NO

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated, senior officials, named principals) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (2026-10-05). Active US-Iran military exchange continued through September 2026. Qatar and Pakistan relay communications were ongoing but no confirmed indirect negotiating session between US and Iranian representatives took place before EOD Sep 17. GlobalSecurity OPREP and live updates confirm no formal indirect session was convened in the Sep 3–17 window. The ceasefire that had briefly existed (Apr 8–Jul 8) had collapsed; no new session framework materialized. Ambiguity rule governs: message relay without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Resolved NO with high confidence.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session (not mere message relay) between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official mediator readout.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Message relay through intermediaries without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump assertions of 'semi-negotiating' without Iranian or mediator confirmation of a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (2026-10-05). IMF PortWatch recorded approximately 1 commercial transit on Sep 27 — against an 85-vessels-per-day pre-war baseline. As of early October, 139 AIS-visible vessels remained holding position outside their berths in the Gulf watch box; five vessel strikes near the Strait were reported in the week preceding Oct 4. Traffic ran at approximately 1–10 vessels/day throughout the full measurement period; the 30-vessel-per-day threshold (7-day rolling average) was never remotely approached. Resolved NO with high confidence; no tracker divergence flag needed (all AIS aggregators consistent).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any AIS-based ship-tracking source (IMF PortWatch, Straits.live, MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: AIS-based tracker + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit; if trackers diverge by >20%, flag AMBIGUOUS.

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE (p 0.42→0.35). Polling through Oct 4 shows a volatile near-tie. Four of five recent polls average Yashar (Eisenkot) at 23–24 seats vs Likud at 21–23, with Yashar holding the multi-poll-average lead. Two individual polls (KAN News, Channel 12, both Oct 4) reversed the average lead, placing Likud at 24 seats and Yashar at 22–23. At the bloc level, the opposition projects ~62 seats vs Netanyahu bloc ~48–55 in most surveys. The October 7 third anniversary cycle (ceremonies, inquiry narrative) has activated anti-Netanyahu constituencies. Probability reduced from 0.42 to 0.35: a near-coin-flip race in individual polls but a clear Yashar edge in the multi-poll average warrants a modest probability reduction rather than parity.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US reach a preliminary written agreement (ceasefire deal-framework, MoU, or joint communiqué confirmed by both parties) before EOD 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Trump publicly rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz proposal on Oct 1 and explicitly threatened resumed strikes post-November midterms. Iran received a US counterproposal and is reviewing it; Deputy FM Gharibabadi confirmed receipt Oct 4, stating 'the ball is in the United States' court.' Trump stated Oct 3–4 he would review Iran's 14-point plan but 'can't imagine it would be acceptable.' The primary sticking point is nuclear sequencing: US insists nuclear program addressed first; Iran insists on sequencing that defers nuclear talks. The ~26-day lull in territorial strikes may reflect an informal political pause. A formal agreement before Oct 27 is possible but probability is very low given Trump's explicit public posture and the Iranian delegation expulsion.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: A public written agreement — including a ceasefire MoU, framework deal, or joint statement establishing conditions for ending hostilities — signed or jointly announced by Iran and the US (or designated mediators with both parties confirming). Unilateral announcements by one party that the other disputes do not qualify. Verbal commitments alone do not qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Resolve YES on confirmation from at least two TIER1 sources (Reuters, AP, AFP, Bloomberg) AND official statements from both US State Department/White House and Iranian Foreign Ministry/IRNA.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If one party announces a deal but the other disputes its terms or existence, resolve AMBIGUOUS. If a deal is announced after Oct 27 but backdated, resolve NO. If negotiations are confirmed active but no deal is concluded by EOD Oct 27, resolve NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Acceptance → p rises to 0.25; constructive counter → p rises to 0.15; hard rejection → p drops to 0.05

indicators.expected_effect: Confirmed session → p rises to 0.20

forecasts.question: Will US forces execute a large-scale (≥24-hour sustained) offensive air campaign against targets inside Iran before EOD 2026-11-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Trump explicitly stated Oct 1–3 that strikes on Iran could resume after the November 4 midterm elections if a deal is not reached. The USS Theodore Roosevelt CSG and Makin Island ARG were dispatched Oct 1 with ~9,000–10,000 additional personnel, joining the George H.W. Bush and George Washington already on station. Senior Trump administration officials met at Camp David Oct 3–4 to discuss Iran war strategy. GlobalSecurity Day 218 confirms 26 consecutive days without a coalition strike on Iranian territory ashore. The lull most plausibly reflects a political pause tied to midterm election calculus. Probability at 0.28: meaningful but below 0.50, reflecting the genuine possibility that Trump's threat is leverage rather than intention and that diplomatic progress could prevent resumed strikes.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: US forces conduct a sustained offensive air campaign lasting at least 24 consecutive hours with multiple sorties targeting hardened military infrastructure, nuclear facilities, or IRGC installations on Iranian territory. A single drone strike on border positions or at-sea interdiction of Iranian vessels does not qualify. Requires CENTCOM press release confirming strikes on Iranian territory.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Resolve YES on CENTCOM official press release confirming strikes on Iranian territory combined with ≥1 TIER1 source corroborating; CENTCOM PR alone suffices if confirmed by DoD official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If US strikes Iranian-aligned proxy forces (Hezbollah, Houthis, PMF) but not Iranian territory, resolve NO. If strikes occur after Nov 10, resolve NO for this forecast. If Iran first strikes US forces triggering a retaliatory campaign, still resolves YES if threshold met. If strikes are coordinated with Israel but US role is confirmed as primary by CENTCOM, resolves YES; if US role is secondary or advisory only with no independent US sortie package, resolves NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Israeli opposition bloc led by Eisenkot's Yashar win ≥61 seats in the October 27, 2026 Knesset election?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast capturing bloc-level outcome distinct from F5 (party-level plurality). Current polling projects the opposition bloc at 58–64 seats — straddling the 61-seat majority threshold. The key variable is Arab List behavior: formal cooperation brings the bloc to 61+; Arab abstention or neutrality leaves it short. Netanyahu's explicit strategy is deadlock (neither bloc reaches 61), which he treats as a governing win that allows him to form a minority caretaker government. Opposition bloc majority win is a plausible but not probable outcome at current polling.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: The bloc of parties publicly committed to supporting Gadi Eisenkot as Prime Minister (core parties: Yashar, Together, Democrats, Yisrael Beytenu, plus any Arab party external support that is publicly committed before election day) wins ≥61 combined seats in the Oct 27 Knesset election per official Central Elections Committee certified results.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Resolve per Israeli Central Elections Committee official certified results. Haaretz, Jerusalem Post, and Times of Israel may serve as preliminary resolution indicators within 72 hours of final results publication.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If opposition bloc wins exactly 61 seats but one member announces defection before government formation, still resolve YES (election result, not coalition formation). If Arab party support is needed to reach 61 and they offer external support rather than formal coalition membership, still count their seats if they publicly committed to the Eisenkot government before election day. If final results are disputed or under recount, delay resolution until certified.

indicators.expected_effect: Consistent ≥61 in average → p rises to 0.45; currently 58–64 range straddles threshold

indicators.expected_effect: Confirmed Arab support commitment → p rises to 0.52

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach ≥15 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) at any point before EOD 2026-11-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast replacing F4 (resolved NO at ≥30/day by Oct 3) with a lower threshold (15/day, ~18% of pre-war normal) and longer horizon (Nov 30). F4 resolved NO convincingly: ~1 transit on Sep 27, 139 vessels waiting outside berths, five strikes in one week near the Strait. This forecast asks whether partial reopening is achievable by Nov 30. Probability at 0.22 reflects: (a) remote but non-trivial chance that Iran-US diplomacy produces a partial deal in the next 56 days, opening a partial Hormuz corridor; (b) Iran's stated goal of reopening Hormuz as part of any deal framework; (c) but Trump's post-midterm escalation threat, the nuclear sequencing gap, and 139 vessels still waiting as structurally opposing forces.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: Commercial (non-military, non-state) AIS-tracked vessels transiting the full Strait of Hormuz corridor achieve a 7-day rolling average of ≥15 vessels/day at any point before EOD Nov 30, 2026, as measured by IMF PortWatch, Kpler, Windward, or an equivalent authoritative AIS aggregator. Vessels struck, diverted, or forced back do not count toward the rolling average. US-escorted convoys: count only vessels that successfully complete the transit.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Resolve via IMF PortWatch published data, Kpler, or MarineTraffic official weekly report. UKMTO VRA reports serve as corroboration. A single-day reading of ≥15 is insufficient; requires 7-day rolling average at ≥15.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If AIS data is unavailable or demonstrably corrupted due to IRGC transponder jamming or spoofing for the measurement period, apply the most conservative credible estimate from available commercial sources. If data is contradictory between sources by >20%, use the average of available TIER1 aggregators.
